lines.text: Could the best open robot model pick one named book out of a packed bookcase?
We tested Pi 0.5 on our robot arm in simulation, on four test suites.
lines.say: We tested pie zero point five on our robot arm in simulation, on four test suites.

lines.text: Its training scene, shuffled layouts, narrower gaps, and heavy, slippery books.
Out of the box, it scored 0 for 20. It crashed into the bookcase.
lines.say: Out of the box, it scored zero for twenty. It crashed into the bookcase.

lines.text: Fine tuned on 251 demos, it went 50 for 50 in the scene it trained on.
lines.say: Fine tuned on two hundred fifty one demos, it went fifty for fifty in the scene it trained on.

lines.text: On shuffled shelves it drops to 72 percent. Narrower gaps: 73. Heavy, slippery books: just 43.
lines.say: On shuffled shelves it drops to seventy two percent. Narrower gaps: seventy three. Heavy, slippery books: just forty three.

lines.text: A scripted expert that knows every pose sets the ceiling: perfect, except heavy books, at 57.
lines.say: A scripted expert that knows every pose sets the ceiling: perfect, except heavy books, at fifty seven.

lines.text: So where do the 39 misses happen? 33 of them, at contact.
lines.say: So where do the thirty nine misses happen? Thirty three of them, at contact.

lines.text: On thick books, the blade tips push the book deeper into the shelf. The pads never touch it.
In narrow gaps, it opens as wide as in training and shoves the neighbors aside.
And heavy books slip out of the fixed grip, for the policy and the expert alike.
The catch: this is simulation, with scripted demos and one training run.
Cameras can't feel slip. Our tactile skin can. That's the next test.
